A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOD-DiT work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching. Revised experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons, but do not prevent comparison of the papers.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation benchmarks on CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo, and Wan2.1, together with ablations, attention analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional ablations, SVG-2 comparisons, reconstruction diagnostics, and experiments with distilled FastWan.

M1.justification: The three-pattern least-squares model, warm-up, historical-map fusion, linear prediction, Top-K masking, and accelerated execution remain substantively unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1. Text-token masking is newly documented, but the PDFs do not establish a procedural change. No distinct algorithmic adaptation is specified for FastWan.

E1.justification: Coverage remains text-to-video generation using VBench. Wan2.1 was already evaluated in v1 Appendix A.1, and CogVideoX remains in v3 Appendix A.2. FastWan adds a model and inference configuration, without establishing a new dataset, domain, population, or task requirement.

E2.justification: v3 adds a verified comparison against SVG-2 on HunyuanVideo in Table 6. The principal comparisons retain MInference, Radial, SVG, and Sparge. LiteAttention is newly discussed and listed as a baseline, but no corresponding reported result can be identified.

E3.justification: Hunyuan evaluation changes from 129 frames at 768×896 on H800 to 117 frames at 768×1280 on A100; Wan changes from 81 frames at 512×832 to 69 frames at 768×1280. v3 adds five VBench dimensions, an 8-step FastWan configuration, matched-sparsity controls, and reconstruction/fidelity/linearity evaluation protocols. The temporal-deviation reference also changes from step 10 to step 12.

E4.justification: v3 adds a no-update control, matched-sparsity comparison with Radial, block-size and warm-up ablations, quantitative mask fidelity, reconstruction-error analysis, and multi-prompt linearity validation. It also examines pattern validity in distilled FastWan and expands temporal-deviation analysis to multiple heads. Existing Top-K and threshold ablations remain; v1's matched-latency SVG result passage is removed.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly reports averages and 95% confidence intervals from 200 error samples per sequence length; v1 showed a curve without uncertainty information. This is a localized addition to diagnostic reporting, not evidence that benchmark generation runs or seeds were increased. Benchmark tables still do not report run-level uncertainty.

E6.justification: Hunyuan and Wan benchmark results are replaced under revised settings: reported MOD-DiT speedups change from 2.29× and 1.96× to 2.05× and 1.75×, respectively, rather than demonstrating same-setting declines. CogVideoX values, including 1.82× speedup, are retained in Table 5. New SVG-2, ablation, and diagnostic results substantially expand the evidence; Table 7 reports FastWan latency of 327 seconds without MOD-DiT versus 210 seconds with it. Figure 4's error values also change.

T1.justification: New Section 4.4 defines spatial, temporal, and global interaction sets and asserts their orthogonality, completeness, and negligible out-of-basis interactions. Appendix A adds mathematical definitions for mask fidelity and reconstruction/fitting errors. These substantially extend the formal content, although the completeness assertion is not proved. The existing least-squares and complexity derivations in Appendices B–C are retained.

C1.justification: The central sampling-free, training-free dynamic-attention contribution remains. v3 promotes theoretical grounding of the pattern model and replaces the headline claims of 1.89× CogVideoX and 2.29× Hunyuan acceleration with 1.75× Wan and 2.05× Hunyuan acceleration. Explicit state-of-the-art VBench wording is softened. The v1 CogVideoX headline differed from its table's retained 1.82× result.

C2.justification: v3 extends the empirical pattern interpretation into claims of an inevitable, sufficient interaction decomposition and universal mid-to-late linearity. It newly interprets the no-update control as evidence that periodic prediction is necessary and argues applicability to distilled models. It removes the conclusion's practical-superiority discussion relative to trainable sparse methods. The short-sequence warm-up limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies full attention for text-token interactions and states that sparse baselines share an inference API. It removes the main text's per-model latent-frame/token counts and explicit ascending-order sorting instruction. The detailed kernel implementation remains substantially unchanged, and neither version supplies new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds LiteAttention discussion and references to SVG-2, DFSAttn, Prompt-to-Prompt, and Plug-and-Play Diffusion Features. References to Sparse Transformers, latent diffusion, and the LPIPS paper are removed. These update the surrounding literature and theoretical motivation, while the main positioning around mixtures versus existing sparse-attention patterns remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, linear-model exposition, portions of the method, and conclusion are substantially condensed or rewritten. Benchmark material and Appendix A are reorganized, and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. This extends beyond wording changes accompanying new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 removes the workflow diagram, relocates the existing mask comparison and CogVideoX table, and combines Hunyuan/Wan results in a wider table with additional metrics. It redraws the approximation-error plot with confidence intervals, replaces the temporal-deviation display with multiple panels, and adds several diagnostic figures and comparison tables. Existing qualitative videos are retained and repacked.

improvement.justification: The new controls, ablations, SVG-2 comparison, and confidence intervals address v1's limited validation. However, important additions introduce unresolved problems: Appendix A.1.8 interprets a lower retained-attention norm as better retention; Figure 14's frequency counts exceed its stated 300 observations; and Section 4.4 asserts orthogonality and completeness although its global interaction set can overlap the others and no proof is supplied. These weaken the new mathematical and statistical support, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment despite the improved diagnostic coverage.
